blurb:
Tennis balls are not a hobby for Buccaneer. They are a way of life. This four-and-a-half-year-old Boxer mix has one true love, and it is a fuzzy yellow ball sailing through the air in his direction. Rope toy, squeaky toy, something weird you grabbed off the clearance shelf at the pet store? He's in for that too. Basically, if it's a toy, he wants it, and he's going to like you better for bringing it.

He's 47 pounds of moderate-to-high energy with a personality that's impossible to miss. The shelter volunteers figured out pretty fast that if you hold a tennis ball over his head, he'll sit perfectly still and stare right into the camera. The dog is practically Instagram-ready on command.

Buccaneer gets along well with other dogs at the shelter, but the person who found him mentioned his previous owner had dogs and there was some tension there. So he's not a guaranteed fit with every dog. The right move is to bring your pup in for a meet and greet before committing. His experience with kids is unknown since he came in as a stray, so a meet beforehand makes sense there too. Housetrained status is also unknown, but for a dog this playful and motivated, a routine will go a long way fast.

He's fully vaccinated, heartworm negative, microchipped, and already neutered. Head to Lewisville Animal Services during visiting hours and ask for Buccaneer.
shelter_hours: Contact shelter for current visiting hours
scoring_notes:
• Tennis ball obsession and Instagram-ready trick make him an instantly shareable, personality-packed newsletter hook
• Fully vetted and neutered with a playful identity that sells itself — low barrier to emotional connection for readers
• Came in as a stray with some dog-tension history, suggesting a relatively recent intake and moderate wait time

blurb:
She came in from animal control a little underweight and carrying a heartworm diagnosis, but Monica has not let any of that slow her down. She's about a year old, 35 pounds of hound mix, and currently in the middle of Mostly Mutts' Prison Pups training program where she's been soaking up everything they teach her. She's going to come out of that program a genuinely well-trained dog.

The volunteers describe her as friendly, sweet, and gentle, and her whole deal is being close to her people. That part matters because Monica does have separation anxiety. She needs a home where someone is around most of the time, whether that's a stay-at-home situation, a work-from-home setup, or someone who can bring her along. She's not a dog who does well alone for long stretches, and that's just honest. She's currently doing shifts at the Mostly Mutts front desk, so if that tells you anything about her temperament, it should tell you a lot.

She gets along well with other dogs and does best with a calm, good-natured dog companion in the house. Kids 15 and up are a better fit since she tends to get excited when younger kids run. She's heartworm positive right now but treatment is coming, so they're keeping adoptions local. A Mostly Mutts trainer will work with you on the separation anxiety piece after adoption, and they offer free lifetime training classes.

Call 770-272-6888 to ask when Monica is available to meet. Mostly Mutts is in Kennesaw, Tuesday through Sunday.
scoring_notes:
• Underdog-turned-desk-volunteer arc is a compelling redemption narrative with built-in emotional momentum
• Prison Pups training program and free lifetime classes transform her separation anxiety from liability into a supported, solvable challenge
• Heartworm treatment pending and behavioral requirements narrow her adopter pool, suggesting she has been and will continue waiting

blurb:
Someone found Neo wandering on railroad tracks and stopped to help him. Good thing they did. After his stray hold at animal control, it came out that he had pneumonia. He got treated, made his way to Mostly Mutts, and kept getting better from there. He's about 8 years old, 15 pounds of Bichon-Poodle mix, and after everything he's been through, the volunteers say he's genuinely happy.

He does need ongoing medication and will require a family that's ready to manage that. That's the upfront reality with Neo. He's a special needs dog. But in exchange, you get a guy who rolls around on the floor when he's excited, sprawls out in sunny spots to look out windows, occasionally decides it's a lap day and climbs right up, and lives contentedly with a full house of other dogs. He went from chasing the cats in his foster home to being pretty calm around them, though they'd want to do a meet with any cats before committing.

He does best with older kids. Small children who startle him could risk a nip, so if you have young ones at home, he's probably not the right fit. But for a quieter household looking for a sweet, funny, low-key little companion who just needs consistent care and some good people to be near, Neo has a lot to give.

Reach out to Mostly Mutts at 770-272-6888 to set up a time to meet him. They're in Kennesaw, open Tuesday through Sunday.
scoring_notes:
• Railroad tracks rescue followed by pneumonia recovery is the most cinematic origin story in the set—impossible not to root for him
• Ongoing medication needs and household restrictions create a narrow adopter profile, making a newsletter spotlight his best shot at visibility
• Special needs senior with a complex history signals a long road ahead without targeted exposure to the right reader

blurb:
Rae came into Mostly Mutts after a genuinely rough situation. She and three other small dogs were pulled from a neglectful home, went through animal control first, and then Mostly Mutts stepped in and got her the care she needed. She's had a spay, a dental, and a mammary mass removal. It took a while to get her healthy. She's there now.

She's about 10 years old, roughly 9 pounds, and her daily priorities are napping, a little exploring, collecting some petting, and then more napping. She's not a lap dog exactly, but she's friendly and sweet and likes people around. She also has some hearing loss, so she responds better to louder commands or a whistle than to a regular voice. Her foster figured out a system pretty quickly: get her attention, tap a leg, and she comes right over. Mostly Mutts offers free lifetime training classes for all adopted dogs and can help you figure out what works best for a hard-of-hearing girl.

She lives with other dogs in her foster home and basically ignores them, which makes her a solid fit for a home that already has a calm, low-key dog. She'd do best with older kids who know to be gentle with a small senior. Cats are unknown.

Rae is in a foster home right now, so reach out to Mostly Mutts at 770-272-6888 or visit their website to start the process. The rescue is in Kennesaw.
scoring_notes:
• Neglect-to-recovery story spanning multiple surgeries is the most emotionally powerful narrative in the candidate pool
• Senior dog with hearing loss in a niche adopter market makes her a high-urgency feature with real stakes for newsletter readers
• Age, medical history, and specialized needs strongly imply an extended shelter and foster timeline with no easy placement in sight

blurb:
Big paws at 1.5 pounds. That's Benny. He's two months old, part of a Shakespeare-themed litter of nine, and his foster says his personality is already very much keeping pace with those oversized feet.

He's friendly and playful, loves a good wrestling match with his siblings, and then when he's had enough, he's happy to shut it down and curl up with his people. He doesn't need to be the center of attention every second, but he definitely wants to be in the room with you. Litter trained, microchipped, and already working his way through his kitten shot series. You'd finish those as he grows, and Mostly Mutts covers his neuter through an approved North Metro Atlanta vet once he's big enough. Local adoptions only.

If you've got a cat at home who's been flying solo for a while, Benny's the kind of kitten who might actually be a good match. He grew up in a house full of siblings so he knows how to share space. Gentle kids are fine too. Submit an inquiry through mostlymutts.org to set up a meeting.
shelter_address: Kennesaw, GA (foster-based rescue; no public facility)
scoring_notes:
• "Big paws, big personality" framing is a natural headline hook with strong visual appeal for print and digital
• Proven sibling compatibility makes him a rare easy pitch for multi-pet households seeking a low-drama addition
• One of nine littermates with no wait-time signals; least differentiated backstory of the three kitten candidates

blurb:
Puck is the smallest of a nine-kitten litter, and he has apparently decided that gives him something to prove. His thing is shoulders. Specifically, climbing onto yours and staying there. At two months old and 1.5 pounds, he's figured out that the best seat in any room belongs to whoever's standing up, and he will find a way up there.

When he's not perched on a person, he's running zoomies until he completely runs out of gas, then immediately looking for a lap to collapse into. He doesn't really do in-between. It's full speed or full snuggle, and both are apparently excellent. His foster says he's reliably the first one to find the best spot in the room, which tracks.

He's litter trained and microchipped. Mostly Mutts will cover his neuter once he's big enough, through an approved vet in the North Metro Atlanta area, so adoptions are local only. He's had his first round of kitten shots and you'd finish those as he grows. If you've got a cat at home who might enjoy a tiny, enthusiastic new housemate, or you've just always wanted a cat who treats you like furniture in the best possible way, submit an inquiry at mostlymutts.org.
shelter_address: Kennesaw, GA (foster-based rescue; no public facility)
scoring_notes:
• Shoulder-climbing, lap-collapsing personality is tailor-made for viral newsletter copy and immediate reader affection
• Lowest barriers of any candidate—tiny, healthy kitten with full rescue support and a clear, charming personality
• Fresh kitten from a large litter with no indication of extended wait, limiting urgency angle

blurb:
Toby's foster family has a nickname for him: "the little artist." At two months old and about 1.5 pounds, he spends a good chunk of his day rolling onto his back and waving his paws in the air like he's painting something only he can see. It's ridiculous. It's adorable. You'd probably film it every single time.

He's playful and sweet, but he's also got a little independent streak that sets him apart from his eight siblings. When the rest of the litter is still going full throttle, Toby quietly excuses himself and puts himself to bed. He knows when he's done. That's a personality, not just a cat behavior, and it makes him genuinely fun to watch.

He's litter trained and microchipped. He hasn't been neutered yet because he's still too small, but Mostly Mutts covers that cost through one of their approved North Metro Atlanta vets once he's big enough, so this is a local adoption only. He's had his first round of kitten shots and you'd finish the series as he grows. If you've got a gentle kid at home or a cat who might enjoy a small, self-possessed little roommate, Toby's worth a visit. Submit an inquiry through the Mostly Mutts website to get started.
shelter_address: Kennesaw, GA (foster-based rescue; no public facility)
scoring_notes:
• "Little artist" quirk and self-sufficient bedtime routine make him instantly shareable content for newsletter readers
• Kitten with low barriers to entry—litter trained, microchipped, neuter covered—removes friction for first-time adopters
• Recently arrived young kitten with siblings still available, signaling little urgency or wait time
